in_latin.name: Nonnatus
in_latin.meaning: natus in novum, newborn in a new life, rebirth through Christ
in_latin.long_meaning: Nonnatus est nomen, quod significat natus in novum, id est, reatus per Christum. Etymologia huius nominis derivatur ab verbo greci, νεννατός, quod significat renatus. In Evangelio secundum Lucam, Christus dicit: 'Nascere te oportet ante Patrem tuum' (Lucas 2:33). Nomen Nonnatus adumbrat conceptum spiritualis renatus, qui nascitur ex Spiritu Sancto et per fidem in Christum. In historia Ecclesiae Christianae, Nonnatus est nomen, quod attribuitur Sanctis et Patronis, qui demonstrant exemplaria virtutum et fidei. Nomen Nonnatus significat transformationem mentis et cordis, qua homo renascitur ex Spiritu Sancto et per fidem in Christum.

in_english.name: Nonnatus
in_english.meaning: born anew, rebirth through Christ, spiritual rebirth, new life in Christ
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nonnatus means born anew, rebirth through Christ, spiritual rebirth, and new life in Christ. This name is derived from the Greek word νεννατός (nennatos), meaning reborn. In the Gospel of Luke, Christ says: 'You must be born again' (John 3:7). The name Nonnatus symbolizes the concept of spiritual rebirth, born from the Holy Spirit and through faith in Christ. In Christian tradition, Nonnatus is a name given to saints and patrons who exemplify virtues and faith. This name signifies a transformation of the mind and heart, where a person is reborn from the Holy Spirit and through faith in Christ.

data.cultural_impact: In the context of the Christian name "Nonnatus", it can be associated with the veneration of saints and their divine birth. This name reflects the belief in the mystical and miraculous event of a saint's birth and acknowledges the role of faith in their lives.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Nonnatus" carries a deep spiritual meaning, emphasizing the transformative power of faith and the idea of being born anew in the eyes of God. It symbolizes the idea of rebirth, renewal, and the indelible mark left on the world by those who embrace the teachings of Christ.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nonnatus means "not born" in Latin. In a Christian context, it symbolizes the concept of being called or chosen by God to serve, even if not born into that role or family. It's a reminder of God's providence and the importance of responding to His call.

historical_references.reference: Saint Nonnatus, a Cornish saint, was reputed to have been born in the fourth century in Glastonbury. According to legend, he was a shepherd boy who was thrown into a well by his wicked stepmother. A dove appeared and healed his wounds. He became a priest and was later consecrated a bishop by Saint Germanus. Nonnatus is the patron saint of healers, midwives, and those who draw water.

Saint Nonnatus, a missionary bishop working in Africa during the late 3rd and early 4th centuries, is remembered for his strenuous efforts to convert the inhabitants of what is now Tunisia to Christianity. He is said to have performed many miracles and was eventually martyred, along with some of his followers, by the Roman authorities. Nonnatus is the patron saint of travelers.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Nonnatus' is most notably recognized from the British television series 'Call the Midwife'. Set in the 1950s and 1960s in the Poplar district of London, the show follows a group of midwives and nurses led by the character Sister Evangelina (played by Pam Ferris), who is also known as Sister Nonnatus. The name Nonnatus is derived from the Latin word 'nonnatus' meaning 'not yet born'. The show has gained a massive following since its debut in 2012 and is available to stream on BBC iPlayer, Netflix, and Amazon Prime Video. The modern context of the name has expanded beyond religious connotations, as it is now synonymous with midwifery and nursing in the 1950s and 1960s in the UK.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Nonnatus from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Nonnatus - "Born or reborn". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
